sections.title: Advanced Concept
sections.content: Level 3 Data Interpretation involves large multi-layered tables with data across multiple years, regions, or categories. Questions require combined calculations such as cumulative totals, weighted averages, percentage contribution, and multi-step comparisons.

sections.title: ₹ Based Advanced Example
sections.content: Suppose a company’s ₹ sales, expenses, and profit for 5 products are given for 4 years. You may be asked to find overall profit percentage for all years combined, identify the year with highest growth rate, or determine the product with maximum contribution to total revenue.

sections.title: Important Concepts and Formulas
sections.content:
1. Overall Profit % = (Total Profit / Total Expense) × 100
2. Successive Percentage Change = a + b + (ab/100)
3. Weighted Average = (Sum of value × weight) ÷ Total weight
4. Contribution % = (Part / Grand Total) × 100

sections.title: High-Level Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Calculating average of percentages instead of actual values
2. Using wrong base year for growth calculation
3. Ignoring weight in weighted average problems
4. Doing lengthy exact calculations when approximation is sufficient

sections.title: Strategic Approach
sections.content:
1. Scan the full table before solving
2. Classify questions as total-based, comparison-based, or percentage-based
3. Solve easier comparison questions first
4. Use approximation and ratio methods to save time
5. Recheck base values in percentage change problems

tricks.title: Combined Percentage Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If increase by a% and decrease by b%, net change = a - b - (ab/100).
tricks.example: ₹100 increased by 20% then decreased by 10% gives 20 - 10 - 2 = 8% net increase

tricks.title: Weighted Average Fast Method
tricks.explanation: If one group has much larger weight, average will be closer to that group’s value.
tricks.example: ₹100 with weight 10 and ₹200 with weight 2 means average is near ₹100

tricks.title: Contribution Ranking Trick
tricks.explanation: Identify the largest total contributor before calculating exact percentage.
tricks.example: If Product A total ₹8000 and B ₹6000, A contributes more

tricks.title: Cross Multiplication Comparison
tricks.explanation: Compare ratios without converting to percentage.

tricks.title: Net Growth Multi-Year Trick
tricks.explanation: For successive increases, apply combined formula stepwise.

tricks.title: Reverse Growth Method
tricks.explanation: To find original after 40% increase, multiply final value by 100/140.

tricks.title: Approximation for Big Numbers
tricks.explanation: Round to nearest 10 or 100 when options are far apart.
tricks.example: ₹19,850 can be treated as ₹20,000 for quick estimation

tricks.title: Difference First Strategy
tricks.explanation: Find absolute difference before converting to percentage.

tricks.title: Elimination Method
tricks.explanation: Use logical elimination when exact calculation is lengthy.
tricks.example: If answer must be above 25%, eliminate smaller options

tricks.title: Time Management Rule
tricks.explanation: Attempt direct comparison questions first and leave heavy calculation ones for later.
tricks.example: Solve highest/lowest type questions before cumulative percentage problems
